On #443 (one source file, `src/schemas/primitives.ts`) the list was 57 of the 195 test files, so a baseline and five mutants ran 57 files six times: about 10 minutes, with four other sessions running on the same laptop. The pull request's own tests are three of those files. A mutant is usually killed by a test that imports its file directly. The wide list matters only for a mutant those tests miss. ```mermaid flowchart LR M["valid mutant"] --> D["round 1: direct importers
(baseline of the same files)"] D -->|"a test fails"| K["killed"] D -->|"all pass"| W["round 2: the wide list
(direct + one module between)"] W -->|"a test fails"| K W -->|"all pass"| S["survivor"] ``` - [ ] `scripts/mutant-tests.ts` prints the direct importers apart from the files one module away (`mutant-tests/core.ts` decides; unit tests for both lists, and for a file with no direct importer). - [ ] Stage 4 runs a baseline of the direct importers and each mutant against them; only a mutant that survives that round runs against the wide list, with its own baseline (made once, the first time a mutant needs it). A survivor is still one that no test in the wide list kills, as today. - [ ] The summary names, per mutant, the round that killed it, and the stage's time. - [ ] Measured: #443's five mutants (head `8b8e1c1a`), before and after, with the times in the pull request. - [ ] A skill change, so the planted-defect sample's review (CLAUDE.md, "Prompts") runs once before merging, and every planted mutant result stays as its README says. - [ ] An ADR (number from the consultant) amending ADR 0054. **See it:** a `/brew-review` of a change to `src/schemas/primitives.ts` reports most mutants killed in round 1, and its stage 4 takes a fraction of the time it took on #443.

and the step's lens, within a budget"] S --> T["Taster's input, beside its lens"] ``` - [ ] Where a Brewery's rules are read: the repository's `.foedrum/house-yeast/` or the Brewery's, as `houseYeast` in `foedrum.jsonc` says (ADR 0018), read with the Brewery's files. - [ ] A brewer with `"houseYeast": true` loads; for each of its attempts the rules whose scope matches the files the batch changed and, when the rule has a `lens`, the step's lens, are given as an input, untrusted like every input (ADR 0041), within a token budget; the selection is recorded with the attempt. - [ ] Reuse the selection of `scripts/house-yeast/core.ts` rather than a second one. - [ ] Red first; an ADR (number from the consultant) amending ADR 0059 and ADR 0018. An attempt's receipt: cost, duration, turns, tokens and denials from its stream ## How it works Each brewer attempt is a `claude -p` run whose `stream-json` output the runner reads line by line (ADR 0042, ADR 0047). Its last event, `result`, carries what the run cost: `total_cost_usd`, `duration_ms`, `duration_api_ms`, `num_turns`, `usage` and `modelUsage` (per model). The captured streams in `test/fixtures/claude-stream/` hold these fields, but nothing in `src/` reads them, so an attempt's end records how it ended and not what it took. The runner also sees each permission denial, and counts them only as a total. A person looking at a batch (the status comment, `foedrum status`, a brewed pull request's "How this was brewed") cannot tell which attempt was expensive, slow, or kept hitting the same refused rule. ```mermaid flowchart LR S["stream: result event
cost, duration, turns, usage per model"] --> E["AttemptEnd: receipt"] D["stream: denials, by tool family"] --> E E --> F["step.finished records it"] F --> C["status comment, status, the PR's brewed table:
one line per attempt"] ``` - [ ] The runner reads `total_cost_usd`, `duration_ms`, `duration_api_ms`, `num_turns`, `usage` and `modelUsage` from `result`, and the edits, tool errors and denials of the run, into a **receipt** on `AttemptEnd`; the driver records it on `step.finished`. A run with no `result` (killed, lost) has a receipt with what was seen, marked incomplete. - [ ] Denials are counted per tool family (`Bash`, `PowerShell`, `Edit`, `Read`, …) with the rule or command prefix that was refused, so an attempt that ends on the environment says which rule kept refusing. - [ ] One line per attempt where a batch is shown: duration, turns, tokens, cost, denials (`implement #1 · 2m 38s · 31 turns · 1.34M tokens · $0.82 est. · 2 denied (Bash)`). Cost is labelled an estimate: on a subscription it is not what the user pays. - [ ] `foedrum status` sums a batch's receipts. - [ ] Red first: unit tests that read each captured fixture into its receipt, and one for a run without `result`. - [ ] An ADR (number from the consultant) amending ADR 0047. **See it:** after a brew, the status comment shows one receipt line per attempt, and `foedrum status ` the batch's total. Feeds #392 (planning tokens apart from brewing), #240 and #442 (the live line). Found while comparing Foedrum with a dashboard that shows a receipt per turn.

Necessity ships as a default diff lens

## How it works

`/brew-review` reviews Foedrum's own pull requests through a Taster per shipped default lens (stage 3 globs `defaults/lenses/diff/*.md`: correctness, security, cross-platform, design conformance, test design), so every Foedrum pull request exercises the prompts Foedrum ships (ADR 0017). Next to them it runs one lens of its own: `necessity` (`.claude/skills/brew-review/lenses/necessity.md`, PR #352).

`necessity` ("every new safeguard needs proof and must not duplicate one in place") applies to any codebase; only its references are Foedrum's (`docs/trust-boundaries.md`, `docs/design/security.md`, the local gate). PR #352 kept it skill-only "like simplify", with no recorded reason. The rule decided on 2026-10-24: **every lens that judges a change ships**. (Simplifying is no longer a lens at all: the Finer, #455, applies it before review, and takes over the skill's stage 2.)

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  N[".claude/skills/brew-review/lenses/necessity.md"] -->|"moved, reworded for any repository"| D["defaults/lenses/diff/necessity.md"]
  D --> BR["/brew-review stage 3"]
  D --> R["a Brewery's recipe: lens diff/necessity"]
```

- [ ] `necessity` moves to `defaults/lenses/diff/necessity.md`, reworded for any repository: proof of need, the layer that already owns the risk ("the repository's trust-boundary or security document, when it has one"), the same work twice, cost against benefit, scope creep. Severity as the other lenses; the other five name it in "Leave to other lenses". `foedrum doctor` lists it in `Defaults in use`.
- [ ] Foedrum's own rule stays where it is: CLAUDE.md's "a new safeguard needs proof" and `docs/trust-boundaries.md` are the documents the shipped lens finds in this repository.
- [ ] `/brew-review` stage 3 tastes through the shipped lenses only; its missing-lens check counts them. Stage 2 is #455's.
- [ ] Exercised before merging: one planted-defect run (`test/fixtures/brew-review/planted-demo`), every planted defect still found, and the necessity lens's findings on it recorded.
- [ ] An ADR (number from the consultant) amending ADR 0022.

**See it:** a Brewery's recipe with `"lens": "diff/necessity"` reviews a change that adds a retry with no observed failure behind it and reports it; `/brew-review` on a Foedrum pull request runs six shipped lenses.

The red proof accepts the regression tests a Gauger names ## How it works Nip's `red` step is the red proof (ADR 0017, ADR 0078): it runs the tests the Gauger committed, before any code changes, and passes only when every one of them fails because the behaviour is missing (`src/checks/red-proof.ts`). A new test that passes fails the proof, and the batch goes back to the Gauger. An order often asks for two kinds of tests. **New-behaviour tests** (`Bash(npm exec *)` is refused) must fail first. **Regression tests** (`Bash(npm run lint)` stays allowed) pin what must keep working: they pass before the change, and that is correct. The red proof knows only the first kind, so the Gauger can either leave the regression tests out, or make them fail some other way. Seen in the third brew (#439, batch `8-1`, #443): the Gauger wrote 16 "stays allowed" tests and listed them as regression tests in its commit message, which the engine does not read; `red #1` failed on them. `gauge #2` then put a refused rule into each of those tests, so each fails because of that neighbour: a test named "keeps `Bash(npm run lint)`" now mixes two cases. ```mermaid flowchart LR G["Gauger's out doc
tests + regressionTests"] --> R{"red proof"} R -->|"a new test passes,
not named a regression test"| F["fails: back to the Gauger"] R -->|"a named regression test fails"| F R -->|"every other test fails for the right reason,
at least one does"| P["passes"] P --> T["testsUnchanged keeps both kinds;
the test-design lens checks the list"] ``` - [ ] The Gauger's out doc names its regression tests (`regressionTests`, by the name the runner reports), apart from the new tests it lists today; `defaults/brewers/gauger.md` says when a test is one: it pins behaviour the order says stays as it is, and passes before the change. - [ ] The red proof accepts a named regression test that passes, refuses one that fails or is skipped, still requires every other new test to fail for the right reason, and still requires at least one such test. A name the report does not list fails the proof, as an unknown test does today. - [ ] The `testsUnchanged` guard keeps the regression tests too, so the Cellarman changes neither kind. - [ ] The test-design lens gets the list and checks each named regression test: it pins behaviour the order keeps, and is not a new-behaviour test named so to pass the red proof. - [ ] The status comment and the pull request's step reports show the regression tests next to the new ones. - [ ] Red first: unit tests of `red-proof.ts` for a passing regression test (proven), a failing one (not proven), a new test that passes (not proven, as today), and a run with regression tests only (not proven). - [ ] An ADR amending 0017 and 0078. **See it:** an order that says "`X` stays as it is" brews with a separate test for `X`, listed as a regression test, and `red` passes on its first attempt. Related: #412 (the pull request's description), ADR 0017, ADR 0078.

The Finer: a brewer that simplifies the change before green and review ## How it works Simplifying changes the code, so it comes before the review that judges the final code: `/brew-review` already works that way (stage 2 simplifies, stage 3 reviews). A recipe does not: Nip goes implement → green → taste, and nothing makes a batch's change smaller before the Taster reads it. A new default brewer, **the Finer** (in brewing, fining clears the haze before the beer is served), simplifies the batch's change and commits it, in one run, between implement and green. Green then checks the Cellarman's and the Finer's work together, and the review reads the simplified code. ```mermaid flowchart LR I["implement
Cellarman"] --> F["fine
Finer: finds + applies + commits,
or nothing to simplify"] F --> G["green: build, typecheck, lint, format, test"] G --> T["taste / review group
on the final code"] T --> PR["open pull request"] ``` Decided with the maintainer on 2026-10-24: - [ ] **`defaults/brewers/finer.md`**, a brewer that produces commits, on the `builder` alias (Sonnet, ADR 0153). It looks for duplication (in the change, and against code the repository already has), dead code, needless indirection and over-general code, and applies the smaller form that does exactly what the code does now. Its list starts from #446's `defaults/lenses/diff/simplify.md` (closed unmerged; the text is on branch `429-simplify-lens`). - [ ] **What it may change:** only files the change already touches; never test declarations or assertions (the `testsUnchanged` guard holds it, ADR 0017); never `package.json`, the lockfile, `.npmrc`, CI, hooks or settings; no change to an error message, an output format or a public interface. It runs the repository's format, lint, typecheck and tests itself before it commits (#432). - [ ] **Nothing to simplify is a valid end:** a `done` with no commit and a reason, amending ADR 0074 for this brewer. - [ ] **Its out doc lists each change** with its file, line and why; the status comment and the pull request's step reports show them. - [ ] **Every default recipe has the step:** Nip gets `{ "id": "fine", "brewer": "finer" }` between `implement` and `green`, and the recipes still to come include it. Green's `onFail` route back to `implement` stays; the ADR says what a failing green after the Finer goes back to. - [ ] **`/brew-review` stage 2 runs the Finer's instructions** instead of `.claude/skills/brew-review/lenses/simplify.md`, which goes: one list of what to look for, used by the recipes and by the skill. Stage 2 still proposes patches the skill tests in its scratch tree. - [ ] No shipped `diff/simplify` lens: a Taster that reported simplifications after the Finer would review what the Finer did. - [ ] Red first: the recipe load with the new step, the Finer's `done` without a commit, and `testsUnchanged` on its attempts. Exercised before merging: the real Finer on a seeded change with a duplicated function and a needless wrapper (as #446's seeded check), and one planted-defect run for the skill change. - [ ] ADR **0166** (the number #446 had), amending ADR 0017, ADR 0074 and ADR 0161. **See it:** a Nip brew whose Cellarman wrote a helper the repository already has: the status comment's path shows `fine #1 ✅`, its report names the duplicate it removed, and green and the Taster run on the smaller change. Overtakes #429 and #446. Related: #452 (necessity ships as a default lens).

A brewer that runs out of turns is retried by resuming its session, keeping its out doc

## Today

A brewer's `maxTurns` goes to claude as `--max-turns` (`src/brewers/claude-command.ts:102`), so claude stops the session at the limit, wherever it is in its work. The runner then fails the attempt as not retryable: "the same budget would run out again" (`src/engine/brewer-runner.ts:270`, ADR 0047). The step's other attempts go unused and the batch is Stuck at once.

Seen on the fourth brew (batch 9-1, #442): the Gauger had committed 45 failing tests and 3 regression tests and written `gauge.md` when it reached 89 turns against 80. Going on took a person four steps: `foedrum retry 9-1`, `foedrum resume 9-1`, a typed prompt in the resumed session ("you ran out of turns, check gauge.md and end"), then `foedrum brew` again. The resumed attempt needed a few turns. The worktree was recreated from the attempt's branch, so the uncommitted `gauge.md` was gone and had to be written again.

"The same budget would run out again" holds for a fresh attempt, not for one that continues the session: that one starts with the work done.

## What to build

ADR 0175 first: it amends ADR 0047 (a budget overrun is retryable when the session can resume) and ADR 0117 (the retry resumes with a prompt of its own, and keeps the attempt's out doc).

- [ ] An attempt that ends on its turn budget, after claude's init report, fails **retryably** when its brewer's session can be resumed (ADR 0117's conditions), so the step's `maxAttempts` apply. Otherwise it stays not retryable, as today.
- [ ] Its retry **resumes that session** whatever the brewer's `retryMode` says, with a short fixed prompt: the attempt ran out of turns; finish what is left of the task, write the out doc, and end. The resumed run gets the brewer's full `maxTurns` again.
- [ ] A resume in the attempt's own worktree keeps the out doc the attempt wrote (uncommitted), when the worktree is still there; when it has to be recreated, the out doc the attempt left is copied back into it.
- [ ] The status comment and the receipt say the retry resumed after a budget overrun.
- [ ] Red first: unit tests of the outcome (retryable only when resumable), of the retry's plan (resume, the prompt), and of the kept out doc, with fake runners and clock. That a budget overrun of a fresh-only brewer stays not retryable is a regression test.

**See it:** a brew whose Gauger runs past `maxTurns` goes on by itself to red, with "resumed after the turn budget" in its status comment.

Related: #442 (where it was seen), ADR 0047, ADR 0117, ADR 0118, ADR 0127.

A brewer step's commits are scanned for secrets when it ends, so its retry can fix them

## Today

The push scan (ADR 0079) runs once, in the `openPullRequest` action, over every commit of the batch. A commit whose added lines look like a secret makes the batch Stuck, and the refusal is kept for the batch's life: a rewind does not scan again, so the batch is cancelled and a person pushes fixed commits or orders it again.

Seen on the fourth brew (batch 9-1, #442): the Gauger's first commit held three key-shaped test fixtures as literals (`AKIA…`, `ghp_…`, a URL with a token query). Every later step built on that commit, and only at the end did the push refuse the batch. The commits had to be rewritten by hand, the batch cancelled, and the pull request opened by hand.

A brewer step's failed attempt never becomes part of the task tree (ADR 0066), so a scan when the step ends would let the step's retry write the fixture as the repository does elsewhere (`['ghp', …].join('_')`), with no rewrite and no person.

## What to build

ADR first (the next free number when this starts): it amends ADR 0079 (the scan also runs when a brewer step's attempt ends) and keeps the push's own scan as the last line.

- [ ] When a brewer attempt that produces commits ends `done`, the runner scans the commits it added (base: the attempt's start), with the same scan as the push (`findSecrets`, the same git environment as ADR 0079). Any finding fails the attempt **retryably**, naming each commit, file and kind, never the matched text (ADR 0088).
- [ ] The retry receives the reason, as every retry does, so its brewer can write the text another way.
- [ ] The push's scan stays as it is.
- [ ] The status comment and the receipt show the reason like any other failed attempt.
- [ ] Red first: unit tests of the attempt's outcome with a fake git and fake commits (one finding fails retryably; none passes; a finding in a commit before the attempt's start is not this attempt's), and that the push's scan still refuses.

**See it:** a Nip brew whose Gauger writes a `ghp_…` literal in a test fails `gauge #1` with "commit …, GitHub token in test/…", and `gauge #2` writes it built at run time; the batch goes on to red.

Keep the machine awake while a brew runs

> **Discuss first.** The direction is agreed, the details aren't: talk them through with the maintainer before writing the prompt or any code.

## Today

A brew runs for many minutes, and `foedrum serve` for hours. Nothing keeps the machine awake: when a laptop's sleep timer fires, every running attempt stops with it, claude and the checks too, and the batch picks up only through the supervisor's lost-attempt path (ADR 0027) once the machine wakes.

## What to build (to settle)

While `foedrum brew` or `foedrum serve` has an attempt running, the machine is kept from sleeping on its idle timer; the display may still turn off. When no attempt runs, or the command ends, the hold is let go.

Each platform has a built-in way (ADR 0004: no package):
- Windows: `SetThreadExecutionState(ES_CONTINUOUS | ES_SYSTEM_REQUIRED)`, held by a small child process for as long as Foedrum runs (for example a PowerShell process that calls it and waits on Foedrum's process id).
- macOS: `caffeinate -i -w <pid>`.
- Linux: `systemd-inhibit --what=idle:sleep --why="foedrum brewing" …` where systemd is there.

**Details to settle in the discussion:** whether it is on by default or a setting in `foedrum.jsonc`; `brew` only, or `serve` too; what happens on battery; what `foedrum doctor` says about it; how the hold is let go when Foedrum is killed (the child watches the parent's process id).

**See it:** start a brew on a laptop with a short sleep timer and walk away: the brew is still running when you come back.

An open pull request is checked again when its base moves, and the result is posted

## How it works

Today a batch fetches its base just before the push (ADR 0090), opens its pull request and is On tap. From then on, Foedrum only waits for `pull_request.ended`. When another pull request merges into the same base first, nobody looks at the open one again:

- **A textual conflict** shows on GitHub as "conflicting", and GitHub then runs no checks on the pull request at all.
- **A semantic break** shows nowhere. The pull request still merges cleanly, but the merged tree no longer builds or passes. GitHub doesn't run a pull request's checks again when its base moves.

Foedrum's design covers only sub-orders of one order: `code` dependencies stack, and bottling merges branches, with conflicts going to the Blender (architecture §3.2). Separate orders brewing in parallel against one repository aren't covered.

Example from Foedrum's own work (2026-10-20): #266 removes `baseFetchRoot` and `openBranchPush`'s `base` option, and makes the worktree fetch reach `https://github.com/<repo>.git`. #269 uses both and fetches from a local scratch remote. #269 merges cleanly into main and would still merge after #266, but the result would fail its typecheck and its demo test. A person found it by reading both diffs.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    M[base branch moves] --> T{merge-tree with the new base}
    T -->|conflict| B[Blender step on that batch]
    T -->|clean| C[checks on the merged tree]
    C -->|fail| F[fix round on that batch, the failing check as input]
    C -->|pass| K[still on tap]
```

## The idea

1. **Prevention, when ordering.** The Innkeeper (#227) flags proposed orders that will touch the same files or modules as an open batch, and suggests an order or "after #X".
2. **Detection, when the base moves.** For each of the Brewery's open pull requests on that base:
   - `git merge-tree` against the new base finds textual conflicts;
   - the repository's checks on that merged tree, in an attempt of their own (ADR 0069), find semantic breaks.
3. **Repair.**
   - A conflict becomes a Blender step on that batch.
   - A failing check becomes a fix round, with the check's output as its input.
   - A choice between approaches ("pick one that works before and after #X") is a `needs_input` question for the Brewmaster (#226), which answers it with a cited source or leaves the batch Stuck with its recommendation.

## Details to settle

- Which event starts it: the state branch seeing a `pull_request.ended` (merged) of the same base, polling the base's tip, or both.
- Whether a batch goes back from On tap to brewing (a new state, or a rewind, ADR 0081), and how the status comment shows it.
- What the checks on a merged tree cost when many pull requests are open, and whether there is a limit or a queue.
- Only the Brewery's own pull requests, or every open pull request on the base.
- **At the push, too.** Before `openPullRequest`, the task tree is compared with the base as it is now, not as it was when the batch started: merge-tree against the fetched base, and the recipe's checks on the merged tree. That way the pull request opens already up to date, with CI on the tree that will land. Settle whether this is a step of its own before the green checks (so they read the merged tree), part of the push effect, or the same mechanism as the base-moved check with the push as one more trigger. (Foedrum's own sessions merge origin/main right before their last push since 2026-10-21, after #288 reported ready while it conflicted.)
- What the Innkeeper compares: the files named in the order, or the files the open batches changed so far.

- [ ] A pull request On tap whose base moves is checked again: merge-tree first, then the repository's checks on the merged tree.
- [ ] Before `openPullRequest`, the task tree is merge-tree checked against the current base, and the checks run on the merged tree.
- [ ] A conflict or a failing check sends that batch back, and its status comment says why.
- [ ] A test starts from two batches whose pull requests merge cleanly one by one but break together, and shows that the second one is sent back once the first merges.

Related: #226, #227, #266, #269.

A repository names its sensitive paths, and a batch that touches one says so

## How it works

Foedrum never merges: a person merges every pull request it opens. Its tasting is just as deep whatever a batch's diff touches: the same lenses, the same models, and Brett's mutation check as the recipe sets it. Nothing tells the person who merges where the risk is.

The idea is to read a few risk signals from each batch's diff. They would set how deep the tasting goes and be shown to the person who merges. They would never approve or block anything themselves.

| Signal | Where it comes from |
|---|---|
| Spread | The diff's files and modules. A sub-order already writes in one repository |
| Tests | Coverage of the changed lines, the red proof, Brett's surviving mutants |
| Sensitive paths | New: path globs per repository in `foedrum.jsonc`, e.g. auth, payments, data migrations, the CI config |

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    D[batch diff] --> S{touches sensitive paths?}
    S -->|yes| T[deeper tasting: security lens on a stronger model, mutation check required]
    S -->|no| N[the recipe's tasting]
    T --> P[status comment and PR body name the paths and signals]
    N --> P
```

## Details to settle

A dismissed finding names the evidence that shows it is not a defect

## How it works

When a Taster's findings send a batch back, the Cellarman records a disposition for each one (ADR 0191). A `dismissed` one needs a `why` that "says why it is not a defect", and the next round "reads it and may contest it once" (`defaults/brewers/cellarman.md`, "A Taster's findings"). - [ ] The prompt's fixture tests follow; no schema change (`why` stays one or two sentences).
- [ ] A line in ADR 0191's follow-up record, or a new ADR if the wording changes what a disposition is.

The same rule for the plan's findings loop is on #391.

Keep a Linux setup's sandbox away from the host's abstract Unix sockets ## How it works This touches the **check sandbox** (`src/platform/check-sandbox.ts`, ADR 0076). It starts a check step's command line in bwrap on Linux and WSL2, with `--unshare-net`, the home folder and `/run` hidden. Since #382 (ADR 0158), a repository's `setup` runs in the same sandbox with the network kept, which on Linux means bwrap without `--unshare-net`: the setup shares the host's network namespace. An abstract Unix socket (a name starting with `@`) belongs to the network namespace, not the file system. So hiding `/run` and `/tmp` does not hide it, and `/proc/net/unix` lists every one of them. A check keeps `--unshare-net` and reaches none. A setup reaches all of them. This issue gives the setup a network namespace of its own, or keeps it from making Unix sockets, so it still reaches its registry and no abstract socket. ```mermaid flowchart LR S[setup in bwrap
host network namespace] -- TCP --> R[registry] S -- today --> A["host's abstract sockets
@/tmp/.X11-unix/X0, unix:abstract= D-Bus"] S -. this issue .-x A ``` ## The proof (CLAUDE.md, Security) The review of #422 (security and cross-platform lenses) found the path. A brewer steered by an injected issue commits a build file that setup runs: a `setup.py` for `pip install`, a `Directory.Build.targets` for `dotnet restore`, a `Gemfile` (ADR 0140, ADR 0158). On Linux that file can then: - connect to an X server's `@/tmp/.X11-unix/X0`. GNOME's XWayland lets the same uid in without a cookie, so the file can type into the user's terminal and run code outside every sandbox; - connect to a D-Bus session bus started with a `unix:abstract=` address (dbus-launch without systemd's user session), where the Secret Service hands out gh's login (ADR 0073). A Cellar whose session bus is systemd's `/run/user//bus` and that runs no X server is not exposed. A desktop Linux Cellar, or a server that starts dbus-launch, is. ADR 0158, "What a setup can still reach", records the gap. **Owner:** the check sandbox, the row "A check step running code a brewer wrote" in `docs/trust-boundaries.md`. This improves the owner and adds no layer. ## What it does - [ ] Pick one, with an ADR (new file only) that amends 0158: - **A user-mode network stack:** keep `--unshare-net` for setup too and give its namespace a network through `pasta` (passt) or `slirp4netns`, attached to bwrap's namespace (`--userns-block-fd` / `--info-fd`). Abstract sockets stay out of reach, and the loopback services of the host go too. Costs: one more tool `foedrum doctor` asks for on Linux, and the wiring that starts it beside bwrap and kills it with the run. - **A seccomp filter:** `bwrap --seccomp ` with a BPF program that makes `socket(AF_UNIX, …)` fail with EPERM (Claude Code's own sandbox does the same for brewers' shell commands). Per architecture (x86_64, aarch64), it refuses foreign syscall ABIs (i386 compat, x32) and lets `socketpair` through, which node and libuv use for child processes. Costs: a hand-built BPF program per architecture, and the process runner passing it on a file descriptor (stdin is unused by setup). It also closes path sockets outside the hidden folders, which a check can reach today. - [ ] The setup stays `unstarted`, never unsandboxed, where the chosen mechanism cannot start. - [ ] Red first with a fake process runner, then an integration case in `test/integration/check-sandbox.test.ts`: the test listens on an abstract socket, and a setup's connect fails. - [ ] ADR 0158's "What a setup can still reach" and `docs/design/platform/isolation.md` lose the gap. ## Today

The local push gate (`scripts/precheck.ts`, ADR 0045) is the guard between a session and the public remote. A code audit of main at `b01300bb` (ADR 0245) found gaps in it, and the review of that audit found one more. All of them still hold at `750bd5cb`.

- **Config-driven pushes.** The same deletes and mirrors can come from git's configuration instead of an option: `git -c remote.origin.mirror=true push origin`, or a plain `git push` after `git config remote.origin.push ':refs/heads/x'` (or a `+` refspec). - **The directory a push starts in.** ADR 0104 runs a push's checks in the tree it pushes, and refuses a directory the command changes into when it is outside the project or a review's scratch clone under `.foedrum/tmp/` (`projectHolds`, `scripts/precheck.ts:1295`), because the gate would run that tree's `npm run check`. The shell's own working directory is never put to that test. Claude Code keeps a session's directory between commands while it stays in the project, so after `cd .foedrum/tmp/review-701` in one command, a plain `git push` in the next runs that clone's check script (someone else's code) before anyone approves the command.

brew-review: a Refactor commit whose test edits only change call arguments is classed mixed

Found in the review of #645 (#621). The maintainer dismissed the result by hand there; this issue makes the review accept the case on its own.

## Today

`/brew-review` stage 1 classes a commit as **refactor** only when it changes `src/` or `scripts/` and touches no test declarations or assertions. A refactor that changes a function's signature has to update the tests' calls in the same commit: a separate test commit before it cannot compile against the old signature, and one after it leaves the refactor commit failing. So such a commit is classed **mixed** and fails the red proof, even when every edit in `test/` only changes call arguments and no expected value changes. Example: #645's "Refactor: the status comment's check lines take the pull request openOf reads" changes `baseCheckLines(batch())` to `baseCheckLines(log.state(), batch())` in its assertion lines. Its message says "The test edits change call arguments only, to the new signatures: no test declaration, assertion or expected value changes".

## What to build

- Stage 1 classes a "Refactor" commit as **refactor** when its test edits only change call arguments or imports in existing tests: no test declaration added, removed or renamed, no expected value changed. The rule that the covering tests are all `ok` at `R^` and at `R` still holds.
- Any other test edit in a refactor keeps the commit **mixed**, as today.
- CLAUDE.md's Tests section gets the matching line. The consultant adds it in a docs PR after the merge.
- Per CLAUDE.md, a skill change is checked with a `/brew-review` run against the planted-defect sample. Add a sample commit of this shape, and keep one that changes an expected value inside a "Refactor" commit so it still fails.


## Widened by the consultant (2026-10-30)

The same session also builds two neighbouring red-proof rules in stage 1. Both have caused blockers the maintainer had to dismiss by hand (#644, #616, #615):
- A **remove** class: a commit whose subject starts with "Remove" deletes code and only the tests of that code (no test is added, no kept test's assertion changes), and the covering tests are `ok` before and after it. It needs no red step and is never the red step for anything.
- "Call arguments or imports" above includes **test helpers** that only change for the new signature.
- A Revert of a commit in the same pull request gets no class of its own. Step 4 names a Remove/Revert pair that nets to the base as a known dismissal case (#644).

A recipe without a gauge step leaves the Cellarman's batch Stuck, even with testFirst false

## How it works

This touches the default Cellarman (`defaults/brewers/cellarman.md`), the brewer that makes a change in one repository, and how its inputs are resolved in a recipe.

The Cellarman declares the input `{ "name": "tests", "from": "step:gauge" }`. A recipe whose `gauge` step is skipped (Nip with `"testFirst": false`, `when: "recipe.testFirst"`) gives it nothing, and the Cellarman runs. A recipe with no `gauge` step at all, even with `"testFirst": false`, cannot resolve the input: the Cellarman's first attempt fails without retry and the batch goes Stuck.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  R["recipe, testFirst false"] --> G{"has a gauge step?"}
  G -->|"yes, skipped by when"| OK["implement runs"]
  G -->|"no"| S["implement fails: input tests needs gauge's out doc"]
  S --> ST["batch Stuck, attempts_exhausted"]
```

## What happens

Found while building #739 (`npm run demo -- ladder`). This Brewery recipe:

```jsonc
{
  "name": "ladder",
  "description": "One change, then its pull request, with no checks",
  "testFirst": false,
  "steps": [
    { "id": "implement", "brewer": "cellarman" },
    { "action": "openPullRequest" }
  ]
}
```

leaves a sub-order's batch Stuck at once, as `foedrum status` shows it:

```
2-1  #2  stuck   attempts exhausted at implement after 1: the scripted brewer could not brew: the input "tests" needs the out doc of step gauge, which has none yet
```

(The "scripted brewer could not brew" prefix is the demo's runner; the reason after it comes from the attempt's plan, before any brewer starts.)

The demo works around it with Nip's own step, `{ "id": "gauge", "brewer": "gauger", "when": "recipe.testFirst" }`, which is skipped.

## What it should do

A recipe without test first that has no `gauge` step should let the Cellarman run without the `tests` input, as a skipped `gauge` step does; or the recipe loader should refuse such a recipe when it loads, naming the missing step, instead of a batch going Stuck at its first attempt. Which of the two is a decision for this issue.

Attempt plans read a step's brewer in the batch's current recipe, not the attempt's

## How it works

This touches the attempt plans (`createAttemptPlans`, `src/brewers/attempt-plans.ts`), which build an attempt's prompt from the brewer of its step and the out docs of earlier steps it names as inputs (`step:<id>`).

A batch's folded steps keep the attempts of every recipe it brewed, since a person can choose another recipe (`foedrum recipe`, ADR 0240). `outDocOf` already reads an attempt's brewer in the recipe that attempt was scheduled under (`attemptRecipeOf`, #657). Two other lookups still read the batch's current recipe, `batch.recipe`:

- `brewerOf`, the brewer of the attempt's own step;
- the `stepBrewer` passed to `inputsOf`, which names the out doc file of the earlier step a `step:<id>` input reads (and, since #774, whether the recipe has that step).

The house-yeast rule `step-recipe-per-attempt` describes this: code that reads a step's definition for an attempt takes the recipe the attempt was scheduled under from the events, never `batch.recipe` alone.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  A["review#1 succeeded under recipe A, its brewer writes review.md"] --> S["a person switches the batch to recipe B"]
  S --> I["B's implement reads step:review"]
  I --> L["the out doc name comes from B's review brewer: tasting.md"]
  L --> X["reads tasting.md in review#1's worktree, which holds review.md"]
```

## What happens

Found in two reviews, #763's and #774's. A case where the two recipes differ:

1. A batch brews recipe A, whose step `review` has a brewer with `output.doc: "review.md"`; `review#1` succeeds.
2. A person chooses recipe B for the batch. B has a step `review` too, with a brewer whose `output.doc` is `"tasting.md"`, and a later step whose brewer has an input `{ "from": "step:review" }`.
3. That later step's plan looks the out doc up through B's `review` brewer and reads `tasting.md` in `review#1`'s worktree, a file A's brewer never wrote. The input fails to read, or reads a stale file of that name.

`brewerOf` has the same reading for an attempt scheduled under one recipe and planned after the batch's recipe changed.

## What it should do

Each lookup reads the brewer in the recipe its attempt was scheduled under: the planned attempt's own for `brewerOf`, and the succeeded attempt's (the one whose worktree the input reads) for a `step:<id>` input's out doc, as `outDocOf` does. A test that switches a batch's recipe between two steps whose brewers write different out docs pins it.

The driver wiring's family and resumes find an attempt's brewer in the batch's current recipe

## How it works

This touches the driver wiring (`src/cli/driver-wiring.ts`), which gives the driver what it asks about each attempt. Two of those questions are `family` and `resumes`:
- `family` is the model family of the attempt's brewer. It decides which closed usage window holds the attempt (ADR 0215).
- `resumes` is whether a retry or an answer continues the session (ADR 0117, ADR 0118).

Both look up the attempt's brewer in the batch's current recipe: `brewerOf(batchId, stepId)` and `recipeOf(batchId)`. `reads`, next to them, already uses the recipe the attempt was scheduled under. Since #792 (ADR 0309), the attempt plans find the attempt's brewer and its `limits` in that recipe too.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  A["brew#1 scheduled under recipe first"] --> S["a person chooses recipe second"]
  S --> P["the plan runs first's brewer (ADR 0309)"]
  S --> F["family asks about second's brewer"]
  F --> W["the wrong usage window holds the attempt, or none does"]
```

## What happens

1. Attempt brew#1 is scheduled under recipe `first`, whose brewer runs on one model family.
2. A person chooses recipe `second` (`foedrum recipe`, ADR 0240) before brew#1 starts. In `second`, step `brew` has a brewer on another family.
3. The plan runs `first`'s brewer, but `family` asks about `second`'s. A closed usage window for the family that actually runs does not hold the attempt, or a window for the other family holds it.

`resumes` can read the wrong brewer's `retryMode` in the same way.
Before #792 every lookup agreed on one recipe. Since then, the plan and these two can disagree.

## What it should do

`family` and `resumes` find the attempt's brewer in the recipe it was scheduled under, through `attemptRecipeOf`, as `reads` does. When the attempt recorded no recipe, they fall back to the batch's recipe.
A test switches recipes between an attempt's scheduling and its start, with brewers on different families or with different retry modes.
A new ADR amends ADR 0309's scope line, which names these two lookups as unchanged.

flowchart LR

A brewer step a route sends back counts its attempts over the batch's life, so its first failure there ends the batch

## How it works

This touches `mayRetry` in `src/engine/recipe-files.ts`, which decides whether a step whose attempt failed retryably gets another attempt or leaves the batch Stuck as `attempts_exhausted`.

A route (`onFail`, `onBlocked` findings, `onPullRequestFail`) schedules a step again after it succeeded.
A plain brewer step counts `attempts.length` over the batch's whole life, successes included, and every default brewer has `maxAttempts` 2.
So after one success and one route back, the step's first failure ends the batch, though only one attempt failed.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  A["implement #1 succeeds"] --> B["correctness asks for changes"]
  B -->|"route back"| C["implement #2 fails once, retryably"]
  C -->|"attempts.length is 2, maxAttempts is 2"| D["Stuck: attempts_exhausted"]
```

#833 fixes this for a lens step, which counts since its latest review (ADR 0324).
This issue is the rest of the defect.

## What a run showed

A scratch run on `9bf3cbd5` of the default Nip with the fake brewer runner, a person's retry being the only way on:

| Scripted | Steps started | Ends |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Cellarman fails once in round 2 | `… correctness acceptance security implement` | Stuck, `attempts_exhausted`, `implement`, 2 attempts |
| The Finer fails once in round 2 | `… implement fine` | Stuck, `attempts_exhausted`, `fine`, 2 attempts |
| The Gauger fails once when Cellarman's findings send it back | `survey survey-check gauge red implement gauge` | Stuck, `attempts_exhausted`, `gauge`, 2 attempts |
| A blocking Brett (a scratch recipe, no default recipe has one) fails once in round 2 | `implement mutate implement mutate` | Stuck, `attempts_exhausted`, `mutate`, 2 attempts |
| `green` reads nothing twice in round 1 and once in round 2 | `… green green green … implement fine green … implement fine green …` | Not Stuck: the third empty read took `green`'s `onFail` round, and the batch went back to Cellarman |

The Maltster's step takes the same branch of `mayRetry`; this run did not script it.
A check step's count is milder: only attempts that read nothing count, over the batch's life (ADR 0069), so successes and failed readings never use it up.
The openPullRequest action already counts per round (ADR 0219).

## What to decide

Whether these steps count since the latest attempt that ended their round, as a plan step (ADR 0289) and a lens step (ADR 0321, ADR 0324) do.
One rule looks like it fits: count the attempts since the latest one that delivered what the step is for, a success or blocked by findings for a brewer step, a reading for a check.
`mayRetry` would then have that one count in place of whole-life, since-success and since-review.

The test `counts a step that writes no plan over the batch: regression test (#731)` in `test/unit/recipe-files.test.ts` pins today's count, and the house yeast rule `re-entered-step-counts-per-round` already asks for the per-round one.
ADR 0053's human `retry` giving one more attempt, and what a route's `maxRounds` bounds, need to stay true under whatever is chosen.

A batch that keeps failing is visible beyond one terminal line

## Today

After #870, one batch's error stops no other batch, and the driver says it once per batch until its message changes or a pass comes clean. That line in the driver's output is the only sign: nobody may be reading that terminal. CLAUDE.md's rule is that a batch must never sit silently, and ADR 0328 keeps a narrowed exception to it, which this issue is to end or settle.

What the #870 session found by reading and testing:

- **`combineEffects.due` is a `flatMap` over its sources**, so one throwing source takes the status comment and labels down with it. A plain guard per source is a trap: `recordAfter` and `noneDue` read "nothing pending" as "all done", so a swallowed source would record `order.decomposed` after an unreadable `planIssues` and let the batch go. The failure has to stay visible to the driver: apply what the other sources give, then fail at the end of the pass. If `planIssues` is the source that throws, the comments naming its sub-issues could be written first.
- **Stuck from brewing already works with a new reason, and is needed there.** A failure in the supervisor hides the attempt's deadline, so an attempt could run past it unseen.
- **Stuck from on tap would make things worse.** `admit` allows it only for `pull_request_failed`, `batch.resumed` never returns a batch to on tap, and `retry` has nothing to schedule. `checkable` and `endable` would then refuse the records of its checks and merge, so its Brewery issue would never close. Allowing it would mean about 200 to 250 lines in the state machine, on the merge path.
- **`foedrum status` reads the fold**, so a person can only see this there if it is an event.

## What to build

The maintainer chose a recorded mark with a limit of 1 hour, and no Stuck from on tap.

- [ ] **The sources stay apart.** One throwing source in `combineEffects.due` leaves the others' effects due, and the pass still fails at its end, so `recordAfter` and `noneDue` never read a swallowed source as "all done". Say what happens when `planIssues` is the source that throws, and pin it.
- [ ] **A batch failing for an hour is marked.** A driver that holds or takes the batch records that it is failing, with the pass and a summary of at most 120 characters (ADR 0099). A clean pass records that it recovered. The mark is a field in the fold and changes no lane. A driver that does not hold the batch records nothing.
- [ ] **A person sees it.** `foedrum status`, `foedrum stuck` and the status comment show the mark. Where the status comment's own source is the one throwing, the comment cannot show it, and `foedrum status` still does.
- [ ] **A brewing batch goes Stuck at the same limit**, with a new reason, because its attempt's deadline may not be readable. `retry` on it does something sensible: say what, and test it.
- [ ] **On tap and the other lanes carry only the mark.** The records of a pull request's checks and its merge still go through, and its Brewery issue still closes. Pin that.
- [ ] **The limit counts from the first failure this driver saw, kept in its memory** (as the flush watch does, ADR 0027), so a restart can make the mark later, never sooner.
- [ ] ADR 0328's exception to "a batch must never sit silently" ends, but for the case named above. The ADR says so, and gives the `CLAUDE.md` line.
- [ ] `effect_failed` and `command_failed` still print every failure: bring them under the print-once line if it is small, or say why not.

**High impact:** these are the engine's most sensitive loops. A session builds this, not `nip`.

**Red tests first, each a new test:** a batch failing for an hour is marked, and one failing for less is not; a clean pass records that it recovered; a driver that does not hold the batch records nothing; a brewing batch goes Stuck at the limit; an on-tap batch with the mark still closes on its merge; a restart makes the mark later, never sooner; one throwing source leaves the status comment posted and the batch not let go.

**Migration:** none in a Brewery's files. A running Brewery reads the added events on restart, and an older Foedrum can't read a state branch holding them, as with any added event. The ADR says so, and a test pins the restart.

1. `foedrum brew foedrum#947` ordered it and at once applied the claim, the Brewery issue, the status comment and `foedrum:ordered`.
2. `foedrum recipe 23 nip "<reason>"` recorded `batch.recipe_chosen` with its reason in the Brewery's state, and applied nothing on GitHub.
3. `foedrum brew 23` recorded the survey's end at once (the Brewery keeps the test map, so no session ran), ran survey-check, started `gauge #1`, and only then applied the status comment, `foedrum:brewing` and `recipe:nip`. GitHub's timeline shows `recipe:nip` about 90 seconds after the choice. An earlier version of this issue said about 11 minutes, estimated from the steps' deadlines; that was wrong, since the survey had no session.

So for that time GitHub said `ordered`, with no recipe, while the batch was brewing. A tick drives first and applies effects after (`src/engine/driver.ts`), and one drive can chain several steps that end at once.

The status comment shows the router's reason (`chosen by the router: <reason>`), but for a person only who and from where: `Recipe nip, chosen by edwin (terminal)` (`recipeText`, `src/engine/status-comment.ts`). The reason `foedrum recipe` requires is in the event and nowhere a person reads it.

## What to build

- [ ] `foedrum recipe` applies the recipe label and the status comment's update itself, before it returns, as ordering applies its effects.
- [ ] The status comment shows a person's reason: `Recipe **nip**, chosen by <who> (<where>): <reason>`, made safe as other brewer and person text is.
- [ ] A brew applies the batch's GitHub effects (status comment, lane label, recipe label) before a step's session starts, so a long step doesn't hold back what the issue shows. Check first how the tick orders driving and applying effects, and say what changes.
- [ ] An ADR.

**See it:** `foedrum recipe <n> nip "<reason>"` leaves `recipe:nip` on the Brewery issue and a status comment that names the reason, before any brew runs. A brew whose first step takes minutes shows `foedrum:brewing` on the issue while that step runs.

**Migration:** none in a Brewery's files. The status comments of open batches with a person's recipe choice are revised once with the reason.

Size: not measured. Expected to be one mechanism: when the effects of a recipe choice and a brew's start reach GitHub, plus one line of text.

The Cellarman handles every Taster's finding, and a person gets only what it can't settle

## Today

Only a step marked blocking sends its findings back. In `nip` that is correctness: acceptance, security and design conformance advise (ADR 0161, ADR 0306, ADR 0343). An advisory finding is written into the status comment and folded inside the pull request's reports, under a line that can read "Ready for review: every Taster approved", and nothing acts on it unless a person reads it and does the work.

On the first real brew with four Tasters (#924), design conformance found that a design page didn't mention the new wording. Nothing acted on it, and it became a follow-up, #925. The same kind of gap showed up on all three orders of the #374 trial.

ADR 0343 kept the Taster advisory because a blocking Taster costs a round and two of its five findings outside the comparison's key were false.

## What to build

The maintainer's rule: **a finding never waits for a person.** Depending on a person to read and act on it means it won't happen.

The direction to discuss:

- [ ] The Cellarman handles every finding of every Taster: it fixes it, or dismisses it with a reason, on the record dispositions already use (ADR 0191).
- [ ] A false finding costs little: it is dismissed with its reason, and the batch goes on.
- [ ] A person gets only what the Cellarman can't settle: a real decision, or rounds that ran out, in plain words (#927).

## To discuss

1. **What runs again after a fix?** One more Cellarman pass and all four Tasters on #924 would be about 1.6M tokens on top of 2.86M, added up from its receipts. Check whether a docs-only fix needs every Taster again, or only the one that asked.
2. **Who checks a dismissal?** A model that wrote the code dismisses a finding about that code. Check what keeps that honest, and whether the Taster that raised it reads the reason.
3. **Rounds:** do all Tasters share correctness's rounds, and what happens when they run out?
4. **Which recipes?** Whether this is the default for `nip`, the full recipe (#915) or every recipe, and what a Brewery's own recipe does.
5. **A finding about something else:** one that was there before the change, or outside the order. ADR 0191 has `pre-existing`. Check whether it still needs a person to file it.
6. **`skip`:** what ADR 0345's lines say once advisory findings no longer exist as such.

This reverses part of ADR 0343 and changes ADR 0161's advisory step, so it needs a decision record of its own.

**Measure before deciding the default:** #915's own measurement can show how many rounds and tokens this costs against what it catches.

**Migration:** to settle in the discussion. A Brewery with its own recipe may need a change.

`/brew-review`'s red proof wants a changed assertion in the red commit (CLAUDE.md). In a brew, the Gauger writes the red commit first and cannot foresee that the fix will change an older test's expected value. `testsUnchanged` guards only the lines the Gauger added, so the Cellarman edits the older test in its own commit. Say what the engine's own red proof, which passed correctly here, should do.

**Discuss first:** nothing starts before a talk with the maintainer.

An ended batch's plan comment is due again when a Foedrum upgrade changes the plan comment's text, and edits the shared order comment with its older plan

## How it works

This is about the plan comment on an order's issue (`src/engine/plan-comment.ts`, ADR 0233, ADR 0275): one comment per order, which every batch of the order edits through the ledger. Each revision records the digest of its text, and `planDue` makes a new revision due when the batch's rendered text no longer matches its own latest revision.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  U["upgrade changes renderPlan's text"] --> P["applyPass asks planEffects of every batch"]
  P --> E["ended batch 7-1: digest differs"]
  E --> C["order comment edited with 7-1's older plan"]
```

## What happens

`applyPass` in `src/engine/driver.ts` walks every batch of the state, ended or not, and asks `planEffects` for its due revisions. When an upgrade changes what `renderPlan` writes for a plan (a new section or a changed line: #658, ADR 0285 and #822's Review section all did), an ended batch's text no longer matches its last revision, so a revision is due for it. Every batch of an order edits the same comment, so when the order was brewed again the first pass after the upgrade edits the order's comment with the ended batch's older plan, until the later batch's next revision.

Scenario: order #7, batch 7-1 planned and was cancelled; batch 7-2 planned again and waits at gate 1. Foedrum is upgraded with a change to `renderPlan`. The driver's next pass finds 7-1's plan comment due and edits the shared comment with 7-1's plan; 7-2's own revision follows only when its text is due again.

What covers part of it today: the order's comment is found by its marker, and a later batch's next revision rewrites it.

## What it should do

Only the plan of the order's latest batch, or of a batch not ended, makes the plan comment due, so an upgrade never puts an ended batch's plan back on the order's comment.

A merge brief can show an earlier recipe's attempt under a step id its current recipe shares

## How it works

This touches the merge brief (`src/engine/merge-brief-post.ts`), the comment a person reads before merging a brewed pull request. Since #868 a brief shows nothing of a recipe its batch left: every line reads only the steps of the batch's current recipe (ADR 0327).

"The current recipe's steps" is decided by step id alone. So an attempt from an earlier recipe still counts as the current recipe's when both recipes have a step of that id, and the brief can report the earlier attempt as evidence on this head.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  A["Earlier recipe: step taste, a Taster, attempt with risk left"] --> B["A person chooses another recipe"]
  B --> C["Current recipe: its own step taste"]
  C --> D{"Did the current recipe's taste run?"}
  D -->|"no, its when is false"| E["The brief shows the earlier attempt's risk and Tasted line"]
  D -->|"yes, a plain step"| F["The brief can read the step as a Taster because of the earlier attempt"]
```

## Today

Found by the review of #868, by reading the code; it has not been run, and nobody has seen it happen.

Two paths, both needing a shared step id across a move with `foedrum recipe`:

- Recipe A has a Taster step `taste`, whose attempt succeeds with a `riskLeft`. Recipe B also has a step `taste`, with a `when` that is false, so it gets no new attempt. The brief shows A's risk under Risk left and a `Tasted at` line from A's attempt, beside a line saying `taste` did not run.
- Recipe A's `taste` is a Taster and recipe B's is a plain brewer step that later succeeds. `tastingSteps` matches any attempt of the step, so the step counts as a Taster, and `tastedLine` reads the plain step's latest attempt as `Tasted at <sha>`.

A step id that is not shared is already left out, and so is a plain step named as a group of the current recipe. So this needs two recipes of one Brewery to reuse an id with a different meaning, which is rarer than the case #868 fixed.

## What to build

- [ ] The brief reads a step's attempts only when the recipe each attempt was scheduled under is the batch's current recipe, taken from the events (house yeast `step-recipe-per-attempt`), not by the step's id alone.
- [ ] Both paths above have a test: neither brief shows the earlier attempt.

**Red test first:** each path above, through `test/unit/merge-brief-mashed.test.ts`'s loaded recipes.

**Migration:** none in a Brewery's files; a brief is only posted, and the events it reads are already recorded.

The intake takes an issue only when someone in users set its label

## Today

The intake takes a target repository's issue when it has the intake labels and was **opened by** someone in the Brewery's `users` (`isCandidate`, `src/engine/issue-claims.ts:76`). Who put the label on doesn't count.

That gets both cases wrong:

- A maintainer can't approve a community member's issue by labelling it. The Cellar skips it in silence, however many labels it gets, and the only way in is by hand with `foedrum brew`.
- Anyone who can label on that repository, such as someone with triage rights, can approve work for a Brewery by labelling an issue a `users` member opened. Opening an issue says nothing about wanting this Brewery to brew it.

## What to build

The maintainer's decision: **the intake label always has to be there, and it has to be set by someone in the Brewery's `users`.** `users` belongs to the Brewery, and is usually one person, its owner, who adds colleagues when a team manages the repository. Creating an issue in a repository doesn't mean a Brewery has to take it.

- [ ] An issue is a candidate only when each of the filter's labels was last added by someone in `users`, whoever opened the issue. Who opened it no longer counts.
- [ ] Who added a label comes from the issue's events: the latest `labeled` event for that label. Read only for an issue that already passes every other check, through the conditional reads (ADR 0052), every page.
- [ ] A label removed and added again counts by its latest adding. A label whose adder can't be told, as with a deleted account, doesn't count.
- [ ] A read of the events that fails leaves the issue out for that pass and says so. It never counts as approved.
- [ ] A person who asks about an issue is told why it's skipped: `foedrum rank` says who set the label, or that nobody in `users` did, in place of "not opened by an allow-listed user". Say what `foedrum status` and the Cellar's output show, without a line every pass.
- [ ] A person's own command is unaffected: `foedrum brew` and `foedrum order` of a target issue are that person choosing it.
- [ ] Say what this does not change, with the reason: a Brewery's own issues (`isBreweryOrder`) and `users` for commands in comments. A comment reaching a brewer stays by association (ADR 0333).
- [ ] `foedrum init` and the docs say this, and that a team adds its colleagues to `users`.
- [ ] An ADR, amending ADR 0043, ADR 0050 and the security page.

**High impact:** this decides who can start work in a Brewery. A session builds it, not `nip`.

**Red tests first, each a new test:**
- `an issue opened by a stranger and labelled by a user is taken`
- `an issue opened by a user and labelled by someone else is not taken`
- `a label a user removed and a stranger added again is not taken`
- `an issue with two intake labels needs both set by users`
- `a read of an issue's events that fails takes nothing`

**Cost:** one more conditional read per candidate per pass, an unchanged answer not counting against the limit. Say the number in the ADR.

**Migration:** no file in a Brewery changes, but what it takes does. An issue labelled by someone not in `users` stops being taken after the upgrade, even if a `users` member opened it: its label has to be set again by someone in `users`. A team adds its colleagues to `users` first. A batch already ordered carries on. The ADR, the pull request and the release notes say so.

A merge brief hides the rounds and the proposed test map of an earlier recipe whose commits are on its head

## How it works

This touches the merge brief (`src/engine/merge-brief-post.ts`), the comment a person reads before they merge a brewed pull request. Since #871 (#970), every line of the brief reads only the attempts scheduled under the batch's current recipe (`ofCurrentRecipe`). But a recipe choice keeps the batch's task tree: each attempt starts where the last success ended (`attemptStart`, ADR 0066), and only a rewind resets it. So an earlier recipe's commits are on the head the brief is about: the fixes its Taster's rounds asked for, and a test map its survey committed. The brief hides both.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  A["Recipe A: a round back fixes code, a survey commits a new test map"] --> B["A person chooses recipe B"]
  B --> C["B starts from A's commits: its survey says fresh"]
  C --> D["Brief today: no round of A, no map line"]
  C --> E["Brief after: A's rounds and the map it proposed are listed"]
```

**Why the scope changed.** This issue first asked for the opposite: that the rounds and survey read only the latest run of the current recipe, so a batch that returned to a recipe would show nothing of its earlier run. The review of #978 found that a recipe choice keeps the task tree, so the earlier run's fixes and its committed map are on the head, and a later survey reads that map as fresh because it is there. Hiding them would leave out a test map no person confirmed, though merging confirms it. The same was already true of an earlier recipe since #970.

## What to build

- [ ] The brief's rounds (`dispositionLines`) and its survey line (`surveyLines`) read the whole batch: every recipe and run it brewed.
- [ ] The lines about a step's latest attempt (`Tasted at`, risk left, open findings, `left open by a skip`, survivors, check steps, steps not run) keep reading the current recipe, as #970 made them.
- [ ] Tests through `test/unit/merge-brief-mashed.test.ts`'s loaded recipes: an earlier recipe's committed map is listed as new; an earlier recipe's fix rounds are listed; a return to the same recipe lists run 1's rounds and map. The #871 tests that expected these left out change in the red commit, with the reason.
- [ ] An ADR records the rule and amends ADR 0327; the design page sentence on the brief follows.

**Migration:** none in a Brewery's files; a brief only reads events that are already recorded.

Found in the review of #970, as its correctness finding 1; rescoped in the review of #978.

A recipe has a type: `mash` or `brew`

## Today

A recipe doesn't say what kind of work it does: `src/schemas/recipe.ts` has no such field. "This recipe plans" is a list of three names, `PLANNING_RECIPES` in `src/schemas/plan.ts`, used in two places: a sub-order may not name one of them, and `foedrum status <order>` counts their tokens as planning.

So a planning recipe a Brewery writes itself isn't recognised as one. The Innkeeper tells a planning recipe from a building one by reading its description (`defaults/brewers/innkeeper.md`). And it may offer every recipe except those that choose a recipe (`src/engine/recipe-files.ts`), so a recipe that isn't for an order at all, such as #921's, looks likely to be offered for a feature. That last point is from reading the code, not from a run: please check it.

## What to build

- [ ] A required `type` on every recipe, `mash` or `brew`. `mash` chooses a recipe or makes a plan and builds nothing. `brew` builds. Later types arrive with their first recipe: #921 `cleanup`, #625 and #284 `audit`. No type without a recipe that uses it.
- [ ] A recipe with no `type` is refused when it loads, with a line that names the file and the fix.
- [ ] `mash-in`, `mash` and `decoction` are `mash`, and `nip` is `brew`.
- [ ] The type replaces `PLANNING_RECIPES` everywhere it's used. Check how a plan's sub-orders can reach the Brewery's recipes, because that check is a static schema today.
- [ ] The Innkeeper is given each recipe's type and uses it to tell planning from building. If its prompt changes, raise its `version`.
- [ ] An ADR records the type, and the design pages and glossary say what each type means.

A type catches the wrong kind of recipe, not the wrong size: `nip` on an issue too big for it still passes. This issue doesn't try to catch that.

## What an existing Brewery must do

A Brewery with its own recipe files adds `type` to each. The ADR and the pull request body give the steps, and the refusal line says the same. Foedrum's own Brewery holds no recipe files, so it has nothing to change.

**See it:** a Brewery recipe of type `mash` under a new name is refused for a sub-order, and `foedrum status <order>` counts its tokens as planning. A recipe with no `type` is refused when it loads.

Size: not measured. Expected to be one mechanism. The default recipe issue and the rename to `deep-mash` both start after this one.

A findings route counts its rounds over the batch's life, so a later run of the recipe gets none

## How it works

This touches a recipe's routes (`src/engine/recipe-files.ts`): a step's `onFindings` route sends the batch back to an earlier step at most `maxRounds` times. `roundsOf` counts the rounds used as the attempts of the route's `goto` step that the route scheduled. It counts them over the batch's whole life. A later run of the recipe, after a person's recipe choice (the same recipe again from Stuck, or a return to it through another) or a rewind, starts with the rounds the earlier run used already spent.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  A["Run 1: taste sends plan back once (maxRounds 1)"] --> B["A person chooses the recipe again"]
  B --> C["Run 2: taste blocks on a finding"]
  C --> D["roundsOf counts run 1's round: 1 of 1 used"]
  D --> E["No round back: Stuck at once"]
```

## Today

Seen while writing the tests of PR #978 (#972), in `test/unit/merge-brief-mashed.test.ts`. A batch of `plain-taste` (taste's `onFindings: { goto: 'plan', maxRounds: 1 }`) used its round in run 1. The person chose `plain-taste` again from Stuck. In run 2, taste blocked on a finding, and the batch went Stuck instead of back to `plan`: the next `run('plan', …)` found plan finished, not scheduled. The tests use `twice-taste`, a copy with `maxRounds: 2`, for this reason.

The code (`roundsOf` in `src/engine/recipe-files.ts`):

```ts
return attemptsOf(batch, route.goto).filter(
  (attempt) => attempt.route !== undefined && from.includes(attempt.route.from) && attempt.route.why === why,
).length;
```

`attemptsOf` takes every attempt of the step, of every run and recipe. `batch.runFrom` (ADR 0357) marks where the latest run from a recipe choice or a rewind began, and `keptRound` and `attemptStart` already count only from it. Not checked: whether the `pull_request` route's rounds (`rounds(batch, from, 'pull_request')`) should reset too, since an open pull request's fix rounds belong to its head.

- [ ] The design pages (`routing`, `commands`) and the glossary say what happens now.

## What an existing Brewery must do

Nothing: with the setting left out, the default is `mash-in`, which ships with Foedrum. The one change a person sees is that `foedrum brew` on an unlabelled issue now starts the Innkeeper, which is one model call, where it used to refuse. The ADR and the pull request body say so.

**See it:** `foedrum brew <n>` on an issue with no label ends at the Innkeeper's question, and the answer chooses the recipe. The same issue under `foedrum serve` still waits.

Size: not measured. Starts after #929, and after pull request #928, because #928 also changes `src/cli/brew.ts`.

An issue edited or commented on after its approving label asks the engineer whether to continue

## Today

Since #903, an issue on a target repository is approved for a Brewery by its intake label, when someone in the Brewery's `users` set it, whoever opened the issue.
The issue's author can still edit its title and body after that, and anyone who can comment can add a comment.
Foedrum reads the order's body again whenever an attempt is planned (`textOf` in `src/brewers/attempt-plans.ts`, `githubOrderText` in `src/github/order-text.ts`, ADR 0333), so text written after the label reaches the brewers.
So the label approves text the person who set it may never have seen. The nonce tags (ADR 0041), the tool allowlists, the sandbox and the person's merge still hold.
Found by the security lens on #903's pull request.

## What to build

Decided by the maintainer (2026-11-10): **when an issue's title or body changed, or a comment was added, after its approving label, Foedrum asks the engineer what to do: continue or not.** It never goes on by itself.

- [ ] Before the intake takes an issue, and before each attempt reads the order, check whether the title or body was edited or a comment added after the latest `labeled` event of the approving label. Say which reads tell this (for example `lastEditedAt`, the `renamed` event, the comments' times), and what each costs per candidate and per attempt, counted.
- [ ] When it was, the batch stops with one question to the engineer, continue or stop, with what changed and a link to the issue, through the surfaces a question already uses (`foedrum stuck`, `foedrum answer`, the status comment). Settle what happens before a batch exists: the intake leaves the issue out and says why in `foedrum rank`, or takes it and asks at once.
- [ ] "Continue" approves the issue as it is at that moment: a later edit or comment asks again. "Stop" ends the batch as a cancel does.
- [ ] Settle which comments count: Foedrum's own comments do not; check whether a comment by someone in `users` should.
- [ ] Test first: new tests for an edited body, an edited title, a new comment, and none of them, each before the code.
- [ ] An ADR that amends the intake's ADR from #903 and ADR 0333; the security page and `docs/trust-boundaries.md` state the rule.

**Before the release:** this lands in M3, before the first published version (#27).

**Migration:** to state in the pull request: a batch already running when this lands may stop at its next attempt with the question, when its issue was edited after its label.

deep-brew: the full recipe's build stage, with all seven diff lenses and Brett

## Today

Foedrum ships four recipes, and one of them builds. `nip` is there to prove a recipe can run, and `mash` to prove one can be selected: `mash` and `decoction` plan and build nothing, `mash-in` asks which recipe to use, and a sub-order can't name any of the three. So every change is built and reviewed by `nip`, however much it can reach.

- `defaults/lenses/diff/` holds seven lenses. `nip` runs four: correctness, acceptance, security and design conformance (#914). No shipped recipe runs cross-platform, necessity or test-design.
- Brett is in no shipped recipe, so mutants run only in `/brew-review`.
- `nip`'s Tasters are on the `builder` alias. The `planner` alias reaches plan lenses only.
- Since ADR 0354, every Taster's findings go back along the step's findings route, in every recipe; only Brett keeps `blocking` (ADR 0319).
- `docs/design/recipes/defaults.md` lists `half-pint`, `pint` and `growler`, and none is shipped.

In #879's final comparison, `nip`'s three Tasters wrote no finding on three brewed heads. On #910, two defects a real review found would have gone through: a feature that recorded nothing while its tests passed, and a fence GitHub would have read as HTML. The comments below record two more cases from the #957 self-brews.

## What to build

**The first work of M3**, decided by the maintainer. Its details were settled with the maintainer on 2026-11-10 (the comments below record each decision).

`deep-brew` is the full recipe's **build stage**. The full recipe has four stages, each added by its own issue in its own milestone: readiness and refine (#373), the build (this issue), the proof (#762) and the documentation (#971).

- [ ] A shipped recipe `deep-brew` (label `recipe:deep-brew`, type `brew` once #929 lands): `nip`'s steps, from the Maltster's survey to the pull request, with its tasting replaced as below.
- [ ] Its tasting: all seven diff lenses together in one Taster step (`lenses`) on the `planner` alias, whose findings go back to the Cellarman as `nip`'s do.
- [ ] A Brett step, `blocking`, whose surviving mutants go back to the Gauger: its round starts at its own latest success without the code (ADR 0358), adds the tests that kill them, the red proof checks they fail, and the Cellarman implements again.
- [ ] Rounds as `nip`'s: two per findings route, then Stuck with the findings open.
- [ ] It replaces the `half-pint`, `pint` and `growler` rows of the design page's recipe table: those names are sizes, and a recipe follows what a change can reach, not its size.
- [ ] A sub-order can name it. The Innkeeper, the Brewmaster and `plan/recipe-fit` choose it by its guidance (#977): what it does, when to choose it, how it is best used. No list of paths, no hard rule; a person confirms the choice.

A plan's testFirst false says a sub-order's test-first is off, but its batch runs its recipe's

## How it works

This touches a sub-order's plan entry and the batch brewed from it. A plan is the Brewmaster's out doc, and each of its sub-orders becomes an order with a batch of its own.

The entry can say `"testFirst": false` with a reason, and the plan comment shows it as `test-first off: <reason>`. The batch reads neither: it runs its recipe's own `testFirst` (`resolveRecipe`), so a person who signs off that line gets a batch that may still run the Gauger.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  A["plan entry: testFirst false"] --> B["plan comment: test-first off"]
  A -.->|"not read"| C["sub-order's batch"]
  D["its recipe's testFirst"] --> C
```

## Today

- By grep in `src/`, a sub-order's `testFirst` and `testFirstOff` are read only by `PlannedSubOrder`'s `superRefine` (`src/schemas/plan.ts`) and the plan comment's `section` (`src/engine/plan-comment.ts`).
- The plan entry a sub-order's brewers read (ADR 0290) repeats the line, so a Gauger can read `test-first off` in a batch that asks it for failing tests.
- A recipe's `testFirst` is what a `"when": "recipe.testFirst"` step reads, and the plan cannot change it.

Found while building #803, whose ADR 0322 refuses `testFirst: false` on a marked sub-order. Until this is settled, that refusal keeps the plan honest and changes no batch.

## What to build

- [ ] Decide which is true: the entry's `testFirst: false` turns the Gauger off for that sub-order's batch, or the field leaves the plan and the Brewmaster names a recipe that is not test-first instead.
- [ ] Make the plan comment and the plan entry say what the batch will do.
- [ ] An older recorded plan with the field still reads.
- [ ] An ADR that records the choice.

**See it:** a scripted plan with `"testFirst": false` on one sub-order, whose plan comment line matches whether that batch ran a `gauge` step.

Related: #803, ADR 0233, ADR 0290, ADR 0322.
